analysis:
This PR changes only documentation: docs/architecture/hardware-support.md (new 'Deadline admission rates' section at head lines 549-580, code-map row at 634) and docs/architecture/inference.md (rate-freshness paragraph near line 872, deadline estimator corrections near lines 1123-1183, code-map row near 2098). No code, wire protocol, key, attestation, authorization, encryption or cache-storage behavior is modified, so no trust boundary (TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-011) is touched by the diff itself.

Security-relevant claims examined: (1) The docs state that first-token deadline admission is a time check only. It changes no KV grant, load quotation, activation floor or memory concurrency, and admitted requests still pass slot and process byte admission. This is consistent with the DoS/memory-admission posture (T-010, T-029) and is described as unchanged. (2) The docs describe a DARKBLOOM_TTFT_ADMISSION_FIXES=0 environment toggle. It only reverts to the previous estimators and is local operator config, with no privilege boundary crossed. (3) The text says the published isolated rate, capacity wire fields and platform memory contract are unchanged, so no coordinator-provider contract drift is documented. (4) Freshness anchoring to the newest observation and the statement that a heartbeat alone never renews evidence are availability and honesty properties of provider-reported capacity. These are self-reported by an adversarial provider (ADV-001) and not trust-bearing in this scope.

Remaining integration questions: the described estimator and MeasuredDecodeStep behavior lives in AdmissionRateEstimators.swift and related Swift files, which are not in this batch. Whether the code matches the docs, and whether the lower isolated-rate floor and anchor could over-admit requests that miss deadlines, is unverified here. It is a performance concern rather than a confidentiality issue. The patch excerpts are truncated but the range maps are complete. No findings, and no threat-model update is needed.
